concerns.location: plan.md:§ Phase Ordering – Phase 4 – Agent Execution
concerns.text: The plan runs the Digital Colleague agent across a factorial set of library sizes (10‑100) with and without Skill‑Pruning, but it does not randomize task order or assign tasks to conditions. Re‑using the same 500 tasks for every library‑size/pruning configuration creates repeated‑measures data that violates the independence assumption of the planned piecewise logistic regression and ANCOVA, threatening causal inference.

concerns.location: research.md:§ 2 – Agent Execution Loop – Composite Success
concerns.text: Success is defined as `Retrieval Precision ≥ 0.8 OR exact solution_path match`. This composite conflates two distinct constructs (retrieval fidelity vs execution correctness) and makes the binary outcome ambiguous, reducing construct validity of the ‘success rate’ metric used for the breakpoint analysis.

The ANCOVA controls only for ‘post‑pruning total redundancy’. Pruning also changes the skill library composition (which skills remain), a potential confound not captured by the redundancy metric, so the causal claim that pruning alone restores performance is not fully supported.

concerns.location: research.md:§ 5 – Compute Feasibility & Data Strategy – Power Check
concerns.text: Power is assessed post‑hoc after data collection. Without an a‑priori power calculation to justify the 500‑task, 10‑size, 2‑pruning, 3‑overlap design, there is no guarantee the study achieves the conventional 0.80 power, leaving the breakpoint estimate under‑powered.

The plan relies on dropping predictors if VIF > 5 after fitting, rather than designing orthogonal predictors beforehand. This reactive approach can alter the model after seeing the data, inflating Type I error and compromising the validity of the breakpoint estimate.
